queries: WITH r AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT f.film_id) AS n FROM film f JOIN inventory i ON i.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), a AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS avg_n FROM r) SELECT SUM(r.n) AS total_films_in_stock, AVG(r.n - a.avg_n) AS avg_above_average FROM r CROSS JOIN a WHERE r.n > a.avg_n

assumptions.assumption: 'Films in inventory' per rating means the number of distinct films that have at least one inventory copy, not the number of physical copies.

The across-rating average is the unweighted mean of the per-rating counts over the ratings that have stock (5 ratings). 'How far above' is the mean of (count - average) over the above-average ratings, unrounded.

alternatives.interpretation: Count physical copies (inventory rows) per rating instead of distinct films.

assumptions.assumption: 'Films in inventory' means distinct films (titles) with at least one copy in inventory, counted per rating. It does not mean physical copies.

The 'average rating' is the unweighted mean of the per-rating film counts across all 5 ratings. The 'how far above' figure is the mean of (rating count - that average) over the above-average ratings, unrounded.

alternatives.interpretation: Count physical inventory copies per rating instead of distinct films.
alternatives.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS n FROM inventory i JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), a AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS avg_n FROM c) SELECT SUM(c.n) AS total_films_in_stock, AVG(c.n - a.avg_n) AS avg_above_average FROM c CROSS JOIN a WHERE c.n > a.avg_n

responses.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT i.film_id) AS n FROM inventory i JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), a AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS avg_n FROM r) SELECT SUM(r.n) AS total_films_in_stock, AVG(r.n - a.avg_n) AS avg_excess_over_average FROM r CROSS JOIN a WHERE r.n > a.avg_n

assumptions.assumption: 'Films in inventory' means distinct films with at least one copy in inventory, counted per rating. Each film is counted once however many copies it has.

The 'average rating' is the unweighted mean of the per-rating film counts across the 5 ratings. 'How far above' is the mean of (rating count minus that average) over the above-average ratings, with no rounding.

alternatives.interpretation: 'Films in inventory' means physical copies (inventory rows) per rating, so a film with several copies is counted several times.
